records.passage: Earth has a geomagnetic field of 30–60 microteslas, and a neodymium-based, rare-earth magnet has a field of about 1.25 tesla, with a magnetic energy density of 4.0 × 105 J/m3.

records.claim: Starquakes on the surface of the magnetar often lead to extremely powerful gamma-ray flare emissions which have been recorded on Earth in 1979, 1998, and 2004.
records.passage: Starquakes triggered on the surface of the magnetar disturb the magnetic field that encompasses it, often leading to extremely powerful gamma-ray flare emissions which have been recorded on Earth in 1979, 1998, and 2004.

narration.text: Why one star's magnetism outweighs lead 10,000 times.
Its field packs more mass-energy than solid metal.
Earth's field is just 30 to 60 microteslas.
A strong neodymium magnet reaches about 1.25 tesla.
Near a magnetar, atoms themselves stretch into thin rods.
Starquakes there have sent gamma-ray flares all the way to Earth.
Up close, chemistry itself would stop working.
So the strongest magnets in the universe are also the deadliest.
